titleStmt.title: The Department of State to the South African Legation

head.hi: The Department of State to the South African Legation

div.p: Negotiations have been pending for a considerable period of time between the Government of the Union of South Africa and the Government of the United States with reference to the conclusion of an Agreement on the Provision of Mutual Aid. The progress of events, and particularly the evolution of the financial situation of the Government of the Union of South Africa, has led the Government of the United States to the conclusion that all forms of mutual aid provided by one Government to the other in the course of the war should be financed at this time by cash payments in both directions.

It is intended that this decision be prospective in effect from February 15, 1944, and that the terms and conditions on which war aid was received by the two Governments from each other before that date be determined in accordance with the principles set forth in the Preliminary Mutual Aid Agreement between the United States and Great Britain, dated February 23, 1942, through an exchange of notes in the form of the draft accompanying this Memorandum.

The supply agencies of the United States Government will continue to be available to the Government of the Union of South Africa for assistance in the handling or facilitating the procurement of necessary supplies in every practicable way.

note.p: Signed at Washington; for text, see Department of State Executive Agreement Series No. 241, or 56 Stat. (pt. 2) 1433. For correspondence on negotiation of the Agreement, see Foreign Relations, 1942, vol. i, pp. 525 ff.
